Because some of the main reasons for the "pay gap" according to people who believe it's a myth, is that women make different career choices than men, don't work the same hours, and take more unpaid time off. Stuff not conducive to profit driven companies.

Because they aren't paid less for the same job. The median salary of women through all jobs is approximately 77% of the median salary of all men across all jobs. When controlled by job, women in the same job as men are paid 93% the salaries of their male counterparts..(Read the conclusion on page 33-34). In some jobs, women have equal pay to men. In some occurrences, the reason for this gap is not a sexist company or boss, but rather that men are more likely to ask for a raise than women are. There's a paper from 2007 on this topic. That's not saying that sexism from corporations doesn't exist, it certainly does and can contribute to the wage gap in some cases, but it certainly doesn't account for 23% difference.

The wage gap is largely a mirror trick. The gap does exist, however, it is heavily affected by factors such as maternity leave and the fact that in a two-parent household the woman is more likely to take the children to the doctor. Males are more attractive to businesses because they appear to be more career orientated, and people see women as more emotional and less logical. Businesses don't hire higher level employees with the sole thought of reducing initial costs, but with the intention of hiring someone who will stay on, be loyal, and exceed expectations. Their hiring is also done by people, not computers, so the approach of "who do I think" is more likely.

My more unpopular opinion is that the gap exists because women are expected to be both at home taking care of the household and at work, but I'm not here to discuss that. I did want to add it as a disclaimer, though.

My experience when I was a working woman is that the pay gap doesn't really exist in most jobs. I experienced far more opportunity gap than anything else. I think many women are like I was and are trapped in support roles in their workplace and denied opportunity for advancement and stuck making poor wages because of it.
